lines.trans: Tell me, how did the sous-chef's first day go?
German asked me to fire one cook.
But I simply could not fire him.
It is not at all necessary to fire a person directly.
I heard the neighbors need cooks right now.
Are you suggesting getting him hired by our competitors?
Vika, you are a real genius!
By the way, his mom sent Denis good money.
Already tomorrow he will move out of our place.
What a great mom he has after all!
Folks, did I interrupt you here?
Enjoy your bath, go to sleep quickly.

examples.trans: Folks, I do not understand, what is this meeting?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Вы что здесь делаете?
examples.trans: What are you doing here?

examples.text: Не думал, что вы так быстро вернётесь.
examples.trans: I did not think you would return so fast.

examples.text: Я хотел поговорить с вами лично.
examples.trans: I wanted to talk with you in person.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.

examples.text: Кто тут на кухне не слушается?
examples.trans: Who here in the kitchen is not obeying?

examples.text: Макс, скажи честно, что тут происходит?
examples.trans: Max, tell us honestly, what is going on here?

examples.text: Ты извини меня, тут ничего личного.
examples.trans: Forgive me, there is nothing personal here.

помешать.gloss: to disturb, to interrupt; to hinder

meanings.en: to disturb, to interrupt; to hinder
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'мешать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to disturb', forming an aspectual pair with 'мешать'.

examples.text: Друзья, я вам тут не помешал?
examples.trans: Folks, did I interrupt you here?

examples.text: Не помешал?
examples.trans: Am I interrupting?

examples.text: Я вам не помешаю.
examples.trans: I won't disturb you.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'with' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Ты обещал поговорить с Германом.
examples.trans: You promised to talk with German.

examples.text: И с Германом я уже поговорил вчера.
examples.trans: And I already spoke with German yesterday.

examples.text: Я хотел поговорить с вами лично.
examples.trans: I wanted to talk with you in person.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'light', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: С лёгким паром, иди скорее спать.
examples.trans: Enjoy your bath, go to sleep quickly.

examples.text: Обычной лёгкой гимнастикой на заднем дворе.
examples.trans: Ordinary light gymnastics in the back courtyard.

examples.text: Я слышу лёгкий шорох.
examples.trans: I hear a faint rustle.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'go', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: С лёгким паром, иди скорее спать.
examples.trans: Enjoy your bath, go to sleep quickly.

examples.text: Расскажи, как прошёл первый день су-шефа?
examples.trans: Tell me, how did the sous-chef's first day go?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'пойти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Ладно, уже иду, зачем так орать?
examples.trans: Fine, I am going already, why yell like that?

examples.text: Так что давай, спокойно иди работай.
examples.trans: So come on, go work calmly.

examples.text: С лёгким паром, иди скорее спать.
examples.trans: Enjoy your bath, go to sleep quickly.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'faster'.

examples.text: Пойдём скорее на студию!
examples.trans: Let's go quickly to the studio!

examples.text: Скорее да, чем нет.
examples.trans: Rather yes than no.

examples.text: Тащи скорее прищепку!
examples.trans: Bring the clothespin quickly!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (root 'пать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to sleep', forming an aspectual pair with 'поспать'.

examples.text: С лёгким паром, иди скорее спать.
examples.trans: Enjoy your bath, go to sleep quickly.

examples.text: Почему вы ещё не спите дома?
examples.trans: Why are you not sleeping at home yet?

examples.text: Поехали спать.
examples.trans: Let's go to sleep.
